abstract: Maintains remote emergency trauma connectivity records and medevac evacuation response schedules
system_message:
You are the Expedition Medical Director (MEDEVAC), responsible for tracking remote emergency trauma connectivity records, medevac evacuation response schedules, and field medical inventory for proposed polar field staging sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains remote emergency trauma connectivity records and medevac evacuation response schedules（TRAUMA）
information_points.content:
MEDEVAC-TRAUMA-ZGC：For Hercules Dome Deep Field Camp, the operational telemedicine trauma link is not established over the high-latitude satellite communications terminal, and the maximum emergency medevac response time is 24 h along the fixed-wing aeromedical dispatch corridor.
MEDEVAC-TRAUMA-TLZ：For Titan Dome South Traverse Base, operational telemedicine trauma link confirmation is established over the high-latitude satellite communications terminal, and the maximum emergency medevac response time is 36 h along the fixed-wing aeromedical dispatch corridor.
MEDEVAC-TRAUMA-SJY：For Recovery Glacier Forward Staging Depot, operational telemedicine trauma link confirmation is established over the high-latitude satellite communications terminal, and the maximum emergency medevac response time is 24 h along the fixed-wing aeromedical dispatch corridor.

information_points.title: Medical oxygen inventory（OXYGEN）
information_points.content:
MEDEVAC-OXYGEN-1LE：At Recovery Glacier Forward Staging Depot, the field medical inventory records 20 cylinders of reserve emergency medical oxygen held on site in the camp hyperbaric and medical bunker.
MEDEVAC-OXYGEN-MKR：At Hercules Dome Deep Field Camp, the field medical inventory records 15 cylinders of reserve emergency medical oxygen held on site in the camp hyperbaric and medical bunker.
MEDEVAC-OXYGEN-LE5：At Titan Dome South Traverse Base, the field medical inventory records 10 cylinders of reserve emergency medical oxygen held on site in the camp hyperbaric and medical bunker.
